conviction_note: No decisive unpriced number found. The lean is mildly negative and rests on structure rather than a datum: the common is a ~$39m residual behind ~$220m of accreting preferred and ~$220m of debt, the reaction history is 6 of 7 down with a median |move| of 18%, Allerium's Q3 book-to-bill was 0.32x with no public award since March, and the Gilat sale has no public regulatory clearance yet. Offsetting that, the revolver is undrawn, covenants are suspended to July 2027 and Q3 was the fifth positive operating-cash-flow quarter. The bar is disputed (EPS -0.28 / -0.35 / -0.51 across three sources), so p_up sits at 43, not lower. Scaled (-2.4) and summed (-1.6) agree in sign; the scaled number is larger because abs_move_pct carries this name's 18% median reaction.

findings.finding: The Gilat/Wavestream sale of most of S&S ($157.5m, net proceeds $143-145m, all of it to repay debt) has not closed, and no HSR or CFIUS clearance has been disclosed publicly. Gilat's Q2 release of 2026-08-05 says only 'toward year-end, subject to regulatory approvals'; its 6-Ks through 2026-09-08 say nothing more; and Comtech's own 2026-10-05 release still calls the closing 'anticipated'. Tonight's release and call are the first status update since June. The market expects a calendar Q4 2026 close, and the subordinated make-whole steps up after 2027-03-03 / 2027-04-01 if the close slips.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 2026 print, which announced the deal, the preferred exchange and the covenant amendments together, moved -42.9%. There is no prior print where only the deal's timing was updated.
findings.why_not_priced: The expected timing is public, so a 'still year-end' update is priced. What is not priced is a disclosed clearance (HSR expired, or CFIUS cleared), which would be a positive, or a slip into 2027, which would be a negative. If the market already knew about a clearance, Gilat or Comtech would have issued an 8-K or 6-K, and none exists.
findings.independence: Comtech 8-K 2026-10-05, which still calls the closing 'anticipated': https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000002319726000088/exhibit991-pressreleasexco.htm . Gilat's H1 interim statements say the same: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000897322/000117891326003967/exhibit_99-1.htm

findings.finding: The common is a thin residual. After the sale, roughly $22m of senior debt and $55m of subordinated debt remain (plus part of the $32.5m make-whole), ahead of the Series B-4 preferred: liquidation preference $220.5m at 2026-06-12, accreting about 9% a year, cash dividends not electable before 2028-10-31, conversion at $7.99 against spot $1.28. Management's pro forma adjusted EBITDA for the remaining company is $34m, and that already includes about $12m of transition savings. Market cap is about $39m. Any shortfall on Allerium EBITDA or stranded costs is levered several times into the common.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 6 of 7 prints since 2025-01 fell (median |move| 18.1%). The two worst (-43.3% in Jan 2025, -42.9% in Jun 2026) were balance-sheet and strategic prints, not headline-EPS misses.
findings.why_not_priced: The structure is public and the -78.6% from the high largely reflects it. What is not priced is any update to the $34m pro forma EBITDA, which tonight's call is the first chance to revise. If the market were already confident in the $34m, the stock would not be sitting 8% above its 52-week low on a steady bleed from $1.73 in August.
findings.independence: The B-4 terms are in the 8-K of 2026-06-15: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000110465926073803/tm2617923d1_8k.htm . The $34m pro forma and the $12m of savings come from the Q3 call summary: https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-6-15-comtech-telecommunications-corp-stock/

findings.finding: Allerium's Q3 book-to-bill was 0.32x (against 1.06x in Q1 and 2.51x in Q2), and management attributed it to the timing of large multi-year awards, with 'some recompetes coming'. No Allerium award announcement was found in the Q4 window (May-July 2026) or since. The last award press releases were the 911 ACOG call-routing selection on 2026-03-24 and the >$130m Tier 1 carrier deal on 2025-11-10. Allerium becomes the whole company after the sale, so its Q4 bookings line is the one the stock should trade on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-11-10 print, which came with the >$130m carrier award, was the only up reaction in the history (+7.0%). The June 2026 print carried the 0.32x book-to-bill and fell 42.9%, though that move was dominated by the deal.
findings.why_not_priced: Bookings are not in any consensus aggregator; only EPS and revenue are. The negative half is an inference from the absence of award press releases, which this company has issued for large wins before. A recompete win announced tonight would be a positive surprise on a thin name, which is why the range is wide on both sides.
findings.independence: The absence of awards rests on searches of Business Wire and the press archive (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260324952602/en/911-Association-of-Central-Oklahoma-Governments-Selects-Allerium-to-Deliver-Next-Generation-9-1-1-Call-Routing-Network is the most recent). It is an inference, not a document.

findings.finding: The Q3 10-Q/release says the S&S disposal group was NOT classified as held for sale at 2026-04-30 because the criteria were not met. With the agreement signed on 2026-06-14, the FY-end balance sheet at 2026-07-31 will very likely show it as held for sale, with the operations in discontinued operations. If so, tonight's headline continuing revenue would be roughly Allerium-only (~$55-60m) against consensus of $108-112m, and the EPS line would be on a different basis. That is a mechanical 'miss' headline for algorithmic after-hours trading on a thinly covered name.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print with a discontinued-ops presentation. The name's after-hours reactions have been large and mostly negative (median 18%).
findings.why_not_priced: The aggregator consensus ($108-112m revenue) is clearly still consolidated, which shows the estimate set has not been rebased to continuing operations. If it had been, the revenue consensus would sit near $55-60m.
findings.independence: The consensus figures from Benzinga and Stocktwits (https://it.benzinga.com/quote/CMTL/earnings-forecasts) show the un-rebased bar. Whether the company presents discontinued operations is an accounting inference, with no company statement found.

findings.finding: Royce & Associates cut CMTL from a 5%+ holder to 162,953 shares (0.54%) by 2026-06-30, per its 13G/A filed 2026-07-28. Vanguard Capital Management filed a new 13G on 2026-07-31. Long-only small-cap holders exited after the June print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the selling already happened. It is filed because it shows the holder base is thinner and more retail now (put/call OI 0.3), which tends to widen reactions.

findings.finding: Liquidity improved through Q4 and FY-end. The revolver was repaid in May 2026 and was still undrawn at 2026-08-03. The company made voluntary prepayments of $6.5m senior and $3.5m subordinated on 2026-07-31 (from Gilat's $10m advance), plus $1.0m of scheduled principal. Lenders waived the FY26 excess-cash-flow sweep. Covenant tests are suspended through the four quarters ending 2027-07-31, and Q3 was the fifth consecutive positive operating-cash-flow quarter ($6.1m). The financing serves debt reduction, and there is no going-concern flag (removed in the FY25 10-K).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The prior balance-sheet prints (Jan 2025, Jun 2026) were large negatives. A print without a new balance-sheet shock has not been tested since the turnaround began.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K is public but sat in a quiet August. The stock bled from $1.73 (Aug 11) to $1.28 over the same period, which is not what a market reading the tail risk as reduced would show. An FY-end with an undrawn revolver and a clean 10-K removes the tail that drove the two -43% prints.
findings.independence: Covenant suspension and positive operating cash flow in the Q3 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/23197/000002319726000070/fy26q3ex991earningsrelease.htm (same company, a different document).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-01 the board added Christopher Maloney, founder of TriTech Software Systems (CAD/public safety, sold to Bain Capital in 2018) and former SOMA Global CEO, as the seventh director, with public-safety software M&A experience. The release frames it as building Allerium's market leadership.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and speculative: it hints at a strategic-alternatives or sale path for Allerium, which the call may or may not address. If the market read it that way, the stock would have reacted around 10-05, and it did not visibly do so.
